newsitem.title: UK: Both Brents clocked, BP gets one in "late pass".
newsitem.headline: Both Brents clocked, BP gets one in "late pass".

text.p: Both Brent crude cargoes nominated from the paper chains were unclaimed at the five o'clock deadline, traders said.
The cargoes due to load April 4-6 were clocked to Wall Street traders Phibro and Aron. The latter then moved its cargo to British Petroleum (BP) in a "late pass", traders said.
BP now has six of the seven April Brents which have turned wet so far.
Brent cargoes are traded on a paper, or forward market until the 1700 London time deadline on the nearest trading day 15 days before their assigned loading date.
A trading company is clocked when it is left with a paper cargo which has turned physical after that deadline and therefore cannot be passed on as part of pre-sold paper cargo deals.
